idiom_name: System.Text.Json POCO binding: unmapped members skipped by default, [JsonExtensionData] to preserve, JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow to opt into strictness
implementation_notes: System.Text.Json already behaves like a tolerant reader for plain POCOs: properties in the payload that do not map to a CLR member are ignored, so a class that declares only the members it consumes survives producer additions without configuration. Missing members are not "defaulted" by the serializer - a member is tolerant of absence only when it is nullable or has an initialiser (or is skipped via JsonIgnoreCondition), which is why the reader class must give every optional member an explicit default. When unknown members must survive a round-trip, capture them in a Dictionary<string, JsonElement> property marked [JsonExtensionData]; since .NET 8 the strict opposite is available per type or serializer via JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow / JsonSerializerOptions.UnmappedMemberHandling, which is the right switch at a trust boundary.
pitfalls: Non-nullable reference types and C# 11 required members still throw when the key is absent: the tolerant behaviour applies to unmapped *extra* members, not to missing required ones.
Property-name matching is case-insensitive by default but exact about spelling: a producer rename silently binds nothing and yields the member's default instead of an error.

[JsonExtensionData] keeps unknown members but reorders them on write (extension data is emitted last) and conflicts with a second extension-data property; if the payload is re-serialised for another consumer, tolerance quietly becomes mutation.
